human_check_steps:
# Check the input language switches

## iOS (iPhone or iPad, Tatakikun built from master)
1. Open the Tatakikun app. Under Set up, read the "Allow Full Access" row; turn Full Access on in Settings (iOS shows its warning).
2. Tap Language packs: Input languages lists English, 中文, 日本語 with switches. Turn 日本語 off; the Language packs row shows 2.
3. In Notes, with the Tatakikun keyboard, type `watashi`: no わたし or 私. Turn 日本語 back on in the app, come back to Notes: 私 わたし are back.
4. Turn English and 中文 off: 日本語's switch cannot be turned off. Turn them on again.
5. Quit the app (swipe it away) and open it again: the switches are as you left them.
6. Turn Full Access off and 日本語 off: the keyboard still shows Japanese (it uses every language without Full Access).

## Android
1. Tatakikun app → Language packs → Input languages: turn 日本語 off; `watashi` gives no Japanese; turn it on again; the last language cannot be turned off.

## macOS (needs the installer from master; reinstalling disconnects Electron apps until they are reopened)
1. Tatakikun's menu in the menu bar lists each installed language with a check mark. Uncheck 日本語: `watashi` gives no Japanese. The last checked language is greyed out.
